rejected.title: Mortality and self-assessed health
card: Maternal mortality
the number of women who die from causes linked to pregnancy or childbirth, compared with the number of live births. It is usually shown per 100,000 live births.
Infant mortality
the number of babies who die before their first birthday, shown per 1,000 live births.
Under-five mortality
the number of children who die before their fifth birthday, shown per 1,000 live births. It includes infant deaths.
Self-assessed health
how people rate their own health, often from excellent to poor, in a survey. It is a personal view, so it can show how people feel about their health when death rates cannot.
rejected.remember: Maternal, infant and under-five rates count deaths in mothers and young children. Self-assessed health shows how people rate their own health.

a.q: Which measure counts children who die before their fifth birthday, including babies who die in their first year?
opts: Under-five mortality rate
Infant mortality rate
Maternal mortality rate
Self-assessed health status
a.why: Under-five mortality covers deaths from birth up to the fifth birthday, so it includes infant deaths. Infant mortality is the tempting option, but it stops at the first birthday.
a.clue: Look for the measure that runs up to age five.

b.q: A researcher studying a Bendigo community has its infant mortality data. Why might she also collect self-assessed health data?
opts: It shows how people feel about their own health
It gives a more objective measure than death rates
It counts the deaths that infant mortality misses
It shows how many children die before age five
b.why: Self-assessed health is a personal rating from a survey, so it can show how people feel about their health, which death rates cannot. The objective option is tempting, but a personal view is not more objective than a count of deaths. It also counts no deaths at all.
b.clue: Think about what a count of deaths cannot tell you.

b.q: A survey in Bendigo finds that most adults rate their health as good or excellent. What does this result describe?
opts: How people see their own health
How many new cases of illness occurred
How many adults died in the past year
How many mothers died in childbirth
b.why: Self-assessed health is a person's own rating of their health, gathered in a survey. The death option is tempting, but mortality rates count deaths, not opinions. The result gives a personal view of health.
b.clue: The adults were asked to rate themselves.

b.best: How people see their own health

problems.detail: 'Mortality rates count deaths in mothers and young children' overgeneralises. Mortality rates in general (point 3) count deaths across a whole population. Only the maternal, infant and under-five rates on this card are limited to mothers and young children.

opts: Under-five mortality rate
Infant mortality rate
Maternal mortality rate
Self-assessed health status

a.clue: Check the age of each child who died, then see which rate covers both.
